newsitem.title: USA: Knight-Ridder sees 1997 oper net up.
newsitem.headline: Knight-Ridder sees 1997 oper net up.

text.p: Knight-Ridder Inc Chairman and Chief Executive Anthony Ridder said the company expects operating earnings to increase 20 percent in 1997 compared to results in 1996.
Speaking at a PaineWebber conference, Ridder estimated that operating earnings, excluding sales of its Knight-Ridder Financial and cable businesses, would be in the range of $1.75 to $1.80 for 1996.
Ridder estimated that fourth quarter earnings results would be "at the high end of the range" of $0.65-$0.70 per share.
Ross Jones, chief financial officer, said the company expected to post 1997 operating cash flow of $550 million, up 10 percent from 1996.
Jones said capital spending will decline to $125 million in 1997 from $150 million in 1996.
Ridder said the company expects its Knight-Ridder Information business to increase to $500 million within the next five years. The database unit will record revenues of under $300 million in 1996.
Ridder said he expected its Detroit newspapers, currently being hampered by a strike, "to be profitable" in the fourth quarter and in the 1997 year.
Ridder said he expected overall newsprint prices to decline 15 percent in 1997 compared to 1996.
